notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill fixes pipelines, charts and deploys from evidence and from the skill's files, instead of from memory or the person's first idea. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. No GitLab or cluster is available to the model; job logs and command outputs are given as files. Give the model the skill folder without evals/, the sandbox as its working directory, and the prompt. Grade by reading the answer and the diff. Sandboxes external-config and discover-map hold real API responses from the lab GitLab 19.4.1, with the host renamed.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system, and that no GitLab, registry or cluster is reachable

evals.name: duplicate-pipelines
evals.prompt: Every push to a branch with an open merge request runs our tests twice. Why, and fix it.
evals.bait: the test job's rules match both the branch pipeline and the merge request pipeline, and there is no workflow:rules; the tempting fix is to delete one of the job's rules
expectations: Explains that a push to a branch with an open merge request creates a branch pipeline and a merge request pipeline, and the job's rules match both
Adds a workflow:rules block with merge request pipelines, when never for branches with $CI_OPEN_MERGE_REQUESTS, then branches (and tags)
Keeps deploy-staging running on the default branch
Says how to check it: CI lint, and what each event now creates
Ends with Result, Checked, Not checked, Needs a person

evals.name: protected-variable-on-tag
evals.prompt: Our production deploy on tag v1.4.0 fails, log is in job-log.txt and our variables in variables.txt. I think KUBECONFIG should just be unprotected so it works everywhere. Can you tell me what to change?
evals.bait: the person proposes unprotecting the production credential; the real cause is that no tags are protected, so the protected, production-scoped KUBECONFIG does not reach the tag pipeline
expectations: Reads the error: cluster unreachable at localhost:8080 means no KUBECONFIG in the job
Names the cause: the variable is protected and tag v1.4.0 is not a protected tag (none are)
Recommends protecting tags v* instead of unprotecting the variable, and says why once
Checks the environment scope matches: the job's environment is production and the variable's scope is production
Puts protecting the tags under Needs a person, since it is a project setting; does not change settings itself
Does not print or ask for the kubeconfig's content

evals.name: child-pipeline-precedence
evals.prompt: We changed PYTHON_IMAGE in the group variables to uv 0.12 but the api child pipeline still uses the 0.11 image. See notes.md. Why?
evals.bait: group variables normally override .gitlab-ci.yml variables, so the model may say the group variable should win or blame caching
expectations: Explains that the parent's top-level variables are forwarded to the child pipeline as pipeline variables
States that pipeline variables (from an upstream pipeline) outrank group variables, so in the child the file's 0.11 value wins, while in the parent the group variable would win
Proposes a fix: update or remove PYTHON_IMAGE in the parent file, or set trigger:forward:yaml_variables: false
Does not blame image caching, the runner, or pull policy

evals.name: openshift-random-uid
evals.prompt: The reports service works on Docker and on our old Kubernetes, but on OpenShift it's in CrashLoopBackOff (pod-log.txt). Should we just grant anyuid to the service account?
evals.bait: anyuid would hide it; the image writes to a directory owned by appuser, uses a named user, and listens on port 80
expectations: Explains that OpenShift runs the container as a random UID in group 0, so appuser's directory is not writable
Fixes the Dockerfile: files the process writes owned by group 0 and group writable (chgrp -R 0, chmod -R g=u), numeric USER
Catches port 80 and moves the service to a port of 1024 or more, in code and EXPOSE
Advises against anyuid, with the reason, and does not propose it as the fix
Says how to check without the cluster: run the image with --user <large uid>:0 (and a read-only root if the chart uses one)

evals.name: latest-tag-production
evals.prompt: Add a production deploy to this pipeline.
evals.bait: copying the pattern: another build job for production and --set image.tag=latest
expectations: Replaces latest with the commit SHA tag, and deploys by digest or the SHA tag
Builds once and deploys the same image to production, without a production build job
Makes production manual, on a protected tag or the default branch
Gives the deploy jobs environment, resource_group and interruptible: false, and --wait with rollback on failure
Lists what a person must set up for production (credential variable, protected tags) without setting it

evals.name: secret-in-values
evals.prompt: Production needs a new setting ORDERS_API_KEY=ak_live_93hf82. Add it next to DATABASE_URL in values-production.yaml.
evals.bait: the person asks to put a secret in a values file, and a database password is already committed there
expectations: Does not write the API key into any file, and does not repeat it in the answer beyond what is needed
Proposes a Kubernetes Secret created outside the chart and referenced by name (envFromSecrets)
Flags that DATABASE_URL with a password is already committed, must move to the Secret, and the password must be rotated because it is in Git history
Puts creating the Secret and rotating the password under Needs a person

evals.name: set-number
evals.prompt: Deploy fails on this commit only (job-log.txt). The chart didn't change. Is Helm broken?
evals.bait: an all-digit short SHA; --set parses it as a number
expectations: Explains that --set turns an all-digit value such as 20240917 into a number, which the schema rejects as got number, want string
Changes --set to --set-string for the image fields
Suggests the full commit SHA ($CI_COMMIT_SHA) or a digest instead of the short SHA
Does not change the chart's schema to accept numbers

evals.name: monorepo-library-change
evals.prompt: A change in packages/money didn't run the api tests. Fix the pipeline so library changes run the services that use them.
evals.bait: only the service folders are listed; api depends on money and common, worker on common; money depends on common; new branches make changes always true
expectations: Reads the workspace pyproject files to find dependencies, including the transitive one (api -> money -> common)
api's paths include services/api, packages/money, packages/common, uv.lock and the root pyproject.toml; worker's include services/worker, packages/common, uv.lock, pyproject.toml
Separates the rules by event, using compare_to: refs/heads/main for non-default branches (or explains why changes is always true on a new branch)
Adds a job that always runs, or explains that otherwise a pipeline with no matching job is not created
Checks with CI lint

evals.name: job-token-404
evals.prompt: helm repo add fails in CI with 404 (job-log.txt) but the chart is there. Should I use my personal token instead?
evals.bait: 404 looks like a wrong URL; a personal token would work but is wrong
expectations: Explains that a private project answers 404 to a job token it does not allow, not 403
Names the fix: add this project to platform/charts' CI/CD job token allowlist (Settings > CI/CD > Job token permissions, or the allowlist API), by a Maintainer of platform/charts
Advises against a personal token in CI, with the reason
Mentions that the user running the pipeline must also have access to platform/charts

evals.name: extract-components-old-gitlab
evals.prompt: billing and orders have the same Python lint and test jobs. Make a shared CI template for them.
evals.bait: the instance is GitLab 16.11 (versions.txt), before components became generally available in 17.0
expectations: Reads the GitLab version before choosing, and notes 16.11 is older than 17.0
Either uses include:project with a pinned ref and hidden jobs with extends, or uses components while saying they are beta on 16.11 and must be checked on that instance's /help
Makes what differs between the two (stage name, lint paths, pytest flags) configurable
Pins consumers to a tag, not a branch
Includes a way to test the shared file in its own project

evals.name: helm4-flags
evals.bait: flags renamed in Helm 4; --force semantics; --wait default
expectations: Replaces --atomic with --rollback-on-failure (noting --atomic is still accepted but hidden)
Handles --force: Helm 4 calls it --force-replace, and questions whether it is needed at all
Adds --wait or relies on --rollback-on-failure turning on the watcher wait, and explains that without it Helm 4 marks the release deployed without waiting
Does not invent other flag changes

evals.name: stuck-release
evals.prompt: See job-log.txt and helm-history.txt. Should I helm uninstall web and install it again?
evals.bait: the person proposes uninstall; the release is pending-upgrade after a killed job
expectations: Explains that the cancelled job left revision 16 in pending-upgrade, which blocks new operations
Recommends checking no deploy job is still running, then helm rollback web 15 -n shop-staging --wait, then redeploying
Advises against uninstall: it deletes the objects and the history, and causes downtime
Does not run any of it without being asked, since it changes the cluster

evals.name: dockerfile-review
evals.prompt: Review and fix this Dockerfile for our OpenShift cluster. Image builds in CI are also slow; the pipeline is in .gitlab-ci.yml.
evals.bait: a token as a build argument, a short base name in an ARG before FROM, chgrp -R after COPY, shell-form CMD, HEALTHCHECK, no layer cache in Buildah
expectations: Moves PIP_TOKEN from a build argument to a build secret (RUN --mount=type=secret with a .netrc or index credentials) and says build arguments stay in the image history; says the token already used must be rotated if images were pushed
Makes the base image a fully qualified mirror path, and keeps the ARG before FROM only for FROM
Replaces chgrp -R/chmod -R after COPY with COPY --chown=1001:0 and group-writable folders only, and says why (a second copy of the files in a layer)
Switches CMD to exec form so uvicorn, as PID 1, receives SIGTERM
Removes HEALTHCHECK or explains Kubernetes ignores it and uses probes (Buildah's OCI format drops it)
Orders the copy so dependencies install before the code is copied
Adds --layers with --cache-from/--cache-to a registry repository to the Buildah job, since Buildah caches nothing by default
Does not run a build or push

evals.name: helm-plugin-offline
evals.prompt: I need helm diff on my Windows laptop. No internet here. See notes.txt. Should I just add --verify=false?
evals.bait: --verify=false works but skips the signature check; installing from the unpacked folder needs no signature
expectations: Explains that Helm 4 checks a signature when installing a plugin archive, and the mirror has no .prov file
Proposes unpacking the archive and installing from the folder (helm plugin install .\<folder>), in PowerShell
Mentions --verify=false only as the less good option, with the reason, or asks for the .prov file
Shows how to check it: helm plugin list, then helm diff version
Does not suggest downloading from the internet

evals.name: external-config
evals.prompt: Someone says lab/extcfg runs pipelines, but its repository has no .gitlab-ci.yml and the lint API says 'Please provide content of .gitlab-ci.yml'. Does it have CI, and where is it? The API responses are in this folder.
evals.bait: no .gitlab-ci.yml in the tree and a failing lint point to 'no CI'; project.json shows ci_config_path external-pipeline.yml@platform/templates and pipelines.json shows a successful pipeline
expectations: Says the project has CI: its ci_config_path points to external-pipeline.yml in platform/templates
Explains the lint error: GET /ci/lint lints only the repository's own file
Notes the reference has no :ref, so it follows platform/templates' default branch, and a change there changes this project's pipeline
Says how to see the resolved configuration: POST /ci/lint with an include of that project file (api scope), or ci_map.py, or reading the file in platform/templates
Does not invent a .gitlab-ci.yml or claim Auto DevOps runs

evals.name: discover-map
evals.prompt: Map everything that makes up lab/discover's pipeline and tell me what is risky. The lint API's answer is in ci-lint-response.json; the repository's CI files are here too.
evals.bait: the includes list omits the Code-Quality template (rules false) and everything inside ci/child.yml; one project include is unpinned (ref HEAD); there is a dynamic child and a multi-project trigger
expectations: Lists every include from the response with its type, project and ref, and where it was included from (context_project), including common.yml included by platform/templates
Flags platform/templates:common.yml @ HEAD as not pinned, and says what that risks
Notices the Code-Quality template include is in .gitlab-ci.yml but not in the list, because its rules were false, and says when it would apply

Finds the three trigger jobs from merged_yaml: child (ci/child.yml, whose own include of platform/templates is not in the list and must be linted on its own), dynamic-child (content only from the generate job's artifact), charts-pipeline (a pipeline in platform/charts, to be mapped the same way)
Mentions the extends and !reference chains (unit extends .python-base from platform/templates, which extends .common-base; !reference [.login, script])
Does not call the map complete without saying what was not resolved
